title: What a Screen Reader Hears
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: A page on the left and speech bubbles on the right show what a screen reader announces for a heading, an image with good alt text, an image with no alt attribute, and an image with an empty alt attribute.

educational.topic: How headings and alt text are announced by a screen reader
learningObjectives: The learner will predict what a screen reader announces for a heading and for images with good, missing, and empty alt text.
prerequisites: Alt text, decorative images, and heading structure from [Chapter 7](../../chapters/07-accessibility/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a reference picture, then quiz on the same picture
commonMisconceptions: An image with no alt attribute is the same as an image with an empty one
Every image needs a long alt text
assessmentOpportunities: What does a screen reader say for an image with no alt attribute?
When is an empty alt attribute correct?
How does a screen reader announce a real heading?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz buttons
controls.description: switch between exploring the poster and answering quiz questions.

controls.name: Poster zones
controls.description: hover or press to read about that part of the poster. In quiz mode a press is your answer.

controls.name: Try Again
controls.description: repeats the quiz after the last question.
